_about: Authored words for the rating sheet, keyed by the slug of each inventory row. The plain lines follow gabe-lens plain mode and are checked by ../workflow-panel/plain-audit.py. Facts are never typed here: the example under each row is computed by gen-rate-sheet.js from the lab's generated facts.

Identity.plain: The endpoint's name and the place it lives.

Endings and decision points — what deter.plain: The ways a request can end and the checks that decide it.

Effects — the database, and what the end.plain: The rows the endpoint reads and changes, and the work it starts outside the database.

In-flight state — ephemeral but alive du.plain: The values that stay alive only while the request runs.

Structures.plain: The shapes of the body that comes in and the body that goes out.

Functions — by how crucial they are.plain: The code that runs, sorted by how much it decides.

Coverage, context, client, findings.plain: The proof from tests, the callers, and the things that look wrong.

method-path.plain: The endpoint's name — the verb and the URL a client calls.

entity-cluster.plain: The feature that owns the endpoint and the URL group it sits in.

declared-status.plain: The success code the endpoint promises in its decorator.

file-line.plain: The file and line where the handler starts.

risk-flag.plain: A warning that the endpoint is unusually large or heavily used.

signature.plain: The handler's outline — async or not, its length, the type it returns.

kinds-of-ending.plain: The families a request's ending can belong to — success, refusal, framework, validation, uncaught.

the-endings.plain: Every distinct way a request to the endpoint can end.

the-stage-an-ending-leaves-from.plain: The stage where a request stops — edge, gate, input, handler, answer or uncaught.

status-code-per-ending.plain: The HTTP number each ending answers with.

own-guards.plain: A check in the handler's own code that refuses the request.

deciding-branches.plain: A branch inside a called function that changes how the request ends.

catches.plain: A try/except that turns a failure into a status — or hides the failure.

switches.plain: A setting or a swapped-in implementation that changes what the endpoint does.

tables-touched.plain: The database tables the endpoint reads or writes.

operation-per-table.plain: The kind of touch each table gets — read, add, update or delete.

fate-of-the-writes-per-ending.plain: The outcome of the writes on one ending — saved, rolled back or left unsaved.

the-moment-a-table-is-touched.plain: The stage and step at which a table is touched.

provisions.plain: A row the endpoint creates before the handler even starts.

race-on-a-unique-key.plain: Two simultaneous requests that insert the same unique key.

idempotency-claim.plain: A key that makes a request safe to send twice.

events-published.plain: An event the endpoint announces, and the other code that runs because it heard it.

tasks-dispatched.plain: Background work the endpoint starts that keeps running after the answer.

outside-services-called.plain: A service outside the app the endpoint calls — an LLM, an identity provider, a payment API.

request-scoped-state.plain: A value set early in the request that later steps rely on — the auth context, a key on request.state.

client-cache-effects.plain: The cached queries the screen drops or refills after the answer.

request-shape.plain: The schema the request body must match.

response-shape-per-ending.plain: The body each ending answers with.

delivery.plain: The way the answer travels — one reply, or a stream that keeps sending.

validation-cases.plain: The rules that make a request body fail with a 422.

the-handler.plain: The function that faces the API and receives the request.

decision-point-functions.plain: A function whose raise or refusal becomes one of the endings.

data-touching-functions.plain: A function that reads, writes or commits to the database.

context-giving-functions.plain: A function that prepares context for the rest — authentication, the session, settings.

little-helpers-with-a-type.plain: A small function that formats, caps or validates one value.

functions-behind-walk-levels.plain: The count of functions reachable behind the handler and the depth of that walk.

coverage-per-condition.plain: The share of endings and guards that a test proves.

cases.plain: The named test cases that prove an ending.

auth-scheme-gate.plain: The login scheme and the function that checks it.

app-band.plain: The middleware every request in the app passes through.

who-fetches-it.plain: The frontend hook that calls the endpoint and the screen that uses the hook.

can-the-client-tell-the-endings-apart.plain: The screen's ability to tell two different refusals apart.

findings.plain: The anomalies the form check found on the endpoint.

the-ordered-chain-per-ending.plain: The numbered steps a request runs through on one ending — each check, call, fork, setting and catch, down to the answer.

the-checks-met-in-run-order.plain: The checks a request met, in the order they ran, each marked as passed or as the one that stopped it.

the-route-that-passes-every-check.plain: The ending that gets past every check, and the single check that stops each of the others.

the-predicate-per-decision-point.plain: The condition behind each fork, in the author's own words.

how-this-table-was-found.plain: The source that says a table is touched — the map's own edge, the steps of a route, or both.

in-flight-values.plain: The values alive only while a request runs, and the ones the server keeps between requests.

response-headers-per-ending.plain: The headers an ending sends back beside its body — a retry delay, a login scheme.

field-rules-of-the-request-body.plain: The rule on each field of the request body — required, a length, a range, a list of allowed values.

roles-per-function.plain: The part each function plays here — facing the API, deciding an ending, touching the data, giving context.

what-the-case-asserts-on-this-condition.plain: The thing a test really checked on a condition — the status, the message, a code, or something else.

case-role-on-this-endpoint.plain: The reason a test came to this endpoint — to test it, or only to set something up for another test.

workflow-step.plain: The step before this endpoint in its named walk, and the step after.

rate-tier.plain: The rate tier this endpoint sits on, tighter, standard or exempt — the cap is its detail.

how-common-this-piece-is.plain: The count of other endpoints that use the same piece, so the odd one out is visible.

where-this-endpoint-sits-in-the-app.plain: The place of this endpoint among all the others — its rank, the middle value and the largest.

why-this-slot-is-empty.plain: The reason a slot is empty — we looked and found nothing, we did not look, or the kind has no such slot.

expected-slots-at-this-stage.plain: The line that says what a stage normally holds for this kind of element.

what-the-screen-does-on-this-ending.plain: The thing the user gets on an ending — a message, a retry, or a redirect.

rule3.plain: A thing that can change the path, the data, the context or the flow.

rule2.plain: A thing that gives context to something rated 3.

rule1.plain: A thing that gets mentioned and never drilled into.

alert.plain: An alert — quiet at rest, shown on the face only when the value is abnormal.

note.plain: A short note that travels with the rating in the copied text.

confirm.plain: A shortcut that accepts my rating for every row of the section you have not touched.

copy.plain: The full text of your ratings, placed on the clipboard for pasting into the chat.

reset.plain: A clean slate — every rating, alert and note of yours is cleared.

card.plain: The spread across the 80 endpoints — smallest, middle and largest.

gap.plain: A fact the map cannot produce yet, so a picture of it waits on new generation work.

detail.plain: The amount of text under each attribute's name.

fresh.plain: A row added after your pass, so its rating is still only my proposal.
